title: This, That, These, and Those in Norwegian
goal: Choose the right Norwegian demonstrative and use the definite noun form after it.

objectives.statement: Choose the right Norwegian demonstrative and use the definite noun form after it.

spans.value: Maja has recently moved into a new flat. Her friend Jonas is helping her look for a few inexpensive things at a second-hand shop. Some objects are beside them; others are farther away, near the back wall.
Se på denne lampa. Den passer på skrivebordet mitt.

blocks.translation: Look at this lamp. It fits on my desk.

spans.value: Ja, men hva med den lampa ved vinduet?

blocks.translation: Yes, but what about that lamp by the window?

spans.value: Den er også fin. Og jeg liker dette speilet her.

blocks.translation: It is nice too. And I like this mirror here.

spans.value: Jeg foretrekker det speilet ved døra.

blocks.translation: I prefer that mirror by the door.

spans.value: Vi trenger også stoler. Er disse stolene komfortable?

blocks.translation: We also need chairs. Are these chairs comfortable?

spans.value: Kanskje, men de stolene bakerst er billigere.

blocks.translation: Perhaps, but those chairs at the back are cheaper.

spans.value: Da kjøper jeg denne lampa og disse stolene.

blocks.translation: Then I’ll buy this lamp and these chairs.

spans.value: Nei, dette lille speilet er lettere å bære!

blocks.translation: No, this small mirror is easier to carry!

blocks.translation: Do you want to buy this lamp?

spans.value: Vi tar ikke de stolene bakerst.

blocks.translation: We’re not taking those chairs at the back.

blocks.translation: No, we’re taking these chairs here.

blocks.translation: Good. This lamp, this mirror, and these chairs.

The next day, Maja is unpacking in her new flat. Jonas stands near several boxes, while Maja points to furniture and objects in different parts of the room.

items.value: a box beside Jonas from a box near the door;

spans.value: Then place the phrases into short practical statements such as:

en.value: This box is going to the kitchen.
That picture is going in the bedroom.
These books are going on the shelf.

spans.value: The new situation changes the purpose. Maja is no longer choosing what to buy; she is identifying where particular belongings should go. The same grammar lets her make each reference clear.

Without looking back at the tables, recall the close forms for masculine or feminine singular, neuter singular, and plural. Then recall the three farther-away forms. Finally, describe one nearby singular object, one farther-away neuter object, and several nearby objects, always using a demonstrative followed by the definite noun form.

prompt.value: The shop has objects beside Maja and Jonas and objects farther away. Choose the interpretation that correctly identifies the close and far demonstratives. Focus on distance, not noun gender or number.

options.text: Beside the speakers: den lampa, det speilet, de stolene. Farther away: denne lampa, dette speilet, disse stolene.
options.why: The close and far sets are reversed.

options.text: Beside the speakers: denne lampa, dette speilet, disse stolene. Farther away: den lampa, det speilet, de stolene.
options.why: The close set is denne/dette/disse; the far set is den/det/de.

options.text: Beside the speakers: denne lampa, det speilet, disse stolene. Farther away: den lampa, dette speilet, de stolene.
options.why: The neuter forms are assigned to the wrong distance.

stem.value: Which interpretation matches the shop scene?

prompt.value: Fill each blank with the demonstrative that matches the noun. Close or far is already stated; focus on noun gender or number.

explanation.value: Use denne/den for common singular, dette/det for neuter singular, and disse/de for plural; the noun remains definite after the demonstrative.

prompt.value: Select the one token that is wrong/needs changing.

payload.feedback: The noun after a demonstrative must be definite: change «stol» to «stolen».

prompt.value: Choose the labels that correctly distinguish all three nearby items.

options.text: denne lampa · dette bordet · disse stolene
options.why: The nearby common singular, neuter singular, and plural forms are denne, dette, and disse, each followed by a definite noun.

options.text: denne lampe · dette bord · disse stoler
options.why: A demonstrative requires the definite noun forms lampa, bordet, and stolene.

options.text: dette lampa · denne bordet · de stolene
options.why: Dette is neuter, denne is common singular, and de points to farther-away plural items.

stem.value: Maja points to one lamp, one table, and several chairs beside her. Which set uses the right demonstrative and noun form for every item?

prompt.value: Complete the phrase for the small table. Choose the demonstrative and the definite noun, keeping the supplied adjective between them.

Write one short Norwegian counter summary with four complete noun phrases: the selected lamp, selected mirror, selected chairs, and rejected chairs at the back. Use the taught demonstrative plus definite-noun pattern, and include bakerst with the rejected chairs.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for every criterion. Accept normal capitalization and punctuation, but require each listed demonstrative to be followed by its definite noun.

criteria.instruction: Uses «denne lampa» for the selected lamp, with definite noun «lampa».
Uses «dette speilet» for the selected mirror, with definite noun «speilet».
Uses «disse stolene» for the selected chairs, with definite noun «stolene».
Uses «de stolene bakerst» for the rejected chairs at the back.

prompt.value: In the unpacking scene, write six short Norwegian placement statements, one for each cue: a box beside Jonas (close), a box near the door (far), a picture in Maja's hands (close), a picture on the far wall (far), books on the nearby table (close), and books across the room (far). Use a complete demonstrative noun phrase in every statement. Use new wording rather than copying any complete sentence from the lesson.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all six cues and report evidence for every criterion. Accept varied natural Norwegian placement verbs and normal capitalization or punctuation. Require the listed demonstrative plus definite noun for the matching cue.

criteria.instruction: Uses «denne esken» for the box beside Jonas, with definite noun «esken».
Uses «den esken» for the box near the door, with definite noun «esken».
Uses «dette bildet» for the picture in Maja’s hands, with definite noun «bildet».
Uses «det bildet» for the picture on the far wall, with definite noun «bildet».
Uses «disse bøkene» for the books on the nearby table, with definite noun «bøkene».
Uses «de bøkene» for the books across the room, with definite noun «bøkene».

prompt.value: Complete three short descriptions. For each one, retrieve both the demonstrative and the definite noun form: one nearby singular lamp, one farther-away neuter table, and several nearby books.
